description: Add bulk/multiple-booking support and localStorage draft crash-safety to the New Booking dialog (src/components/dashboard/new-booking-dialog.tsx). Sales users can queue several bookings (each with its own full field set: location, plan, amounts, client, payment, etc.) before a single 'Save all', and any in-progress form + queued bookings survive an accidental refresh/tab-close via a namespaced, per-user localStorage draft that persists until the user explicitly discards it or a successful save clears it. The existing single-booking flow (fill one, Save) must keep working byte-for-byte. This is one coherent feature confined to a single file (no DB migration; bookings table already has all columns).
steps: STEP 0 - Read the whole file first (~1660 lines) to internalize the `f` form-state object, the derived-value block (vo, voGst, addOn, addOnGst, total, quoted, discount, tdsPct, tdsAmt, afterTds, spPay, addOnPay, profit, month, isPartial, amountReceived, balanceAmount), the `submit` useMutation, resetForm(), the T() helper, and the three AlertDialogs (ack email, doc assign). Reuse existing conventions; do not restructure unrelated code.

STEP 1 - Extract a pure row-builder. Refactor the body of `submit.mutationFn` so the per-booking work is a reusable async function, e.g. `async function persistBooking(form: BookingForm): Promise<{ bookingId: string; bookingUuid: string | null; sheet: {ok:boolean; note?:string} }>`. Inside it: (a) resolve the booking id: if form.booking_id starts with 'EMO-BK-' (the local fallback) OR is empty, call `getNextBookingIdFromSheet()` and use its nextBookingId; if that returns null, throw an Error with its .error message (do NOT write a fallback id to the sheet). (b) Compute all derived values FROM `form` (do not read the outer-scope derived consts, which are bound to the live `f`); factor the derivation math (num(), *0.18, tds, profit=(vo+addOn)-spPay-addOnPay, salesMonth) into a small helper `deriveBooking(form)` returning {vo,voGst,addOn,addOnGst,total,quoted,discount,tdsPct,tdsAmt,afterTds,spPay,addOnPay,profit,month,isPartial,amountReceived,balanceAmount} so both the live single-save path and the batch path use identical math. (c) supabase.from('bookings').insert({...same column mapping as today, using form.* and derived.*...}).select('id').single(); throw on error. (d) build the same `values` array as today and `await syncBookingToSheet(values)`. Return {bookingId, bookingUuid, sheet}. CRITICAL ORDERING for batch id uniqueness: because getNextBookingId only marks an id 'used' after a row is appended to the sheet, persistBooking MUST fully await syncBookingToSheet (the sheet append) before the NEXT booking's persistBooking calls getNextBookingIdFromSheet(). Run the batch strictly sequentially (for-await loop), not Promise.all, so each booking gets a distinct sequential id. Preserve the existing single-save behavior exactly by having the single-save path call this same persistBooking with the current form.

STEP 2 - Add queue state. Introduce `const [queue, setQueue] = useState<BookingForm[]>([])` where BookingForm is the type of `f` (define `type BookingForm = typeof initialForm` or an explicit interface; keep it exported-local). Add an 'Add another booking' button in the dialog footer area (next to Save) that: validates the current form with the SAME validation predicate already used to gate the Save button (client_name, contact_no, plan_name, vo_amount, emailOk, contactOk, altOk, alt2Ok, and partial-payment fields when isPartial), pushes a deep copy of the current `f` into `queue`, then resets the form for the next entry via a variant of resetForm() that ALSO fetches a fresh booking id (call refetchNextId() and clear booking_id to a fresh genBookingId() fallback so the next entry does not visually reuse the previous id; the authoritative id is assigned at save time anyway). Show a toast like 'Added to queue (N)'.

STEP 3 - Render the queue list inside the dialog (above or below the form, matching existing spacing/border/muted styling like the 'Payment Received' box). For each queued booking show a compact summary row: client_name, plan_name, city/state, total amount, payment type. Each row has: a Remove button (setQueue removing that index) and an Edit button that loads that queued entry back into `f` for editing and removes it from the queue (so re-adding puts the edited version back). Keep it keyboard/click accessible using existing Button variants. Only render the queue section when queue.length > 0.

STEP 4 - Add 'Save all' behavior. When queue.length > 0, the primary button becomes 'Save all (N)' (or keep 'Save Booking' when queue is empty for the unchanged single path). On Save all: build the list to persist = [...queue, currentForm] BUT only include the current form if it passes validation AND is non-empty (if the current form is blank/partial, save just the queue; if it is filled, include it as the last booking). Iterate SEQUENTIALLY with for-await, calling persistBooking(form) for each inside a try/catch, accumulating results into succeeded[] and failed[] arrays ({index, client_name, error}). Do not abort the whole batch on one failure - continue to the next. After the loop: invalidate ['bookings'] and ['booking-next-id'] once. Surface partial failure clearly: if failed.length === 0 -> toast.success('Saved N bookings' + sheet note); if some failed -> toast.error/'warning' listing how many succeeded and how many failed with the failed client names/errors, AND KEEP the failed bookings in the queue (remove only the succeeded ones) so the user can retry without re-entering data, and KEEP the draft (do not clear localStorage) so nothing is lost. Only clear the queue + form + draft when ALL succeed.

STEP 5 - Post-save behaviors for batch. Preserve the single-booking path EXACTLY (ack-email dialog + doc-assign dialog + partial reminders unchanged) when queue is empty and it is the classic single save. For the BATCH path (queue non-empty), choose a sane, documented behavior to avoid a dialog storm: after a fully-successful Save all, show ONE summary toast and DO NOT open the per-booking ack-email/doc-assign modals for every booking (that would be N stacked dialogs). Instead, still SCHEDULE the partial-payment balance reminders per booking (reuse the existing reminder-insert logic, parameterized by that booking's form + resolved bookingId + bookingUuid) because those are silent inserts, not modal interactions. Document this choice in a code comment and in the handoff. (Rationale: doc-assignment and the ack email were designed around a single booking's modal; running N modals is bad UX. Keeping reminders is safe and preserves data integrity.) Ensure the batch path never crashes if bookingUuid is null (guard like the existing code does).

STEP 6 - localStorage draft persistence. Add a namespaced, per-user key: `const draftKey = user?.id ? `emo:new-booking-draft:${user.id}` : 'emo:new-booking-draft:anon'`. Define a versioned shape: `{ v: 1, form: BookingForm, queue: BookingForm[] }`. (a) SAVE: whenever `f` or `queue` change (useEffect with debounce ~400ms via setTimeout/clearTimeout, or a small throttle) AND the dialog is/was open, write JSON.stringify of the current {v:1, form:f, queue} to localStorage under draftKey. Guard with try/catch (storage can throw in private mode). Do NOT persist the transient sales_agent defaults in a way that overwrites the logged-in user incorrectly on restore - restore form fields but re-apply the current user's sales_agent/sales_agent_id after load (they are set by the existing profile/user effect). (b) RESTORE: on mount / when the dialog first opens, read draftKey, JSON.parse inside try/catch; validate shape (typeof parsed === 'object', parsed.v === 1, parsed.form is an object, Array.isArray(parsed.queue)); merge restored form over the initialForm defaults field-by-field (tolerate missing/extra fields - use `{...initialForm, ...(parsed.form ?? {})}` and filter queue entries through the same merge) so a stale/invalid shape can never crash the form. If a draft with a non-empty queue or a meaningfully-filled form is restored, show a subtle toast ('Restored your saved booking draft') once. (c) KEY BY USER: when user.id changes, do not blindly load another user's draft into the current session; read from the current user's key only. Optionally clear/ignore the anon key after a real user id is known.

STEP 7 - Discard affordance. Add a clearly-labeled 'Discard draft' control (e.g. a ghost/destructive-outline Button in the dialog, shown when there is a draft OR when queue.length>0) that: clears the queue, resets the form (resetForm), and removes the draftKey from localStorage (try/catch). Confirm before wiping if a queue exists (a small window.confirm or reuse AlertDialog is fine; window.confirm is acceptable and simplest). This satisfies the user's requirement that the draft persists until THEY delete it themselves ('jab tak delete naa karo khud se').

STEP 8 - Clear-on-success wiring. On a fully-successful Save all (all succeeded), OR on the existing single-booking success terminal paths (the places that currently call resetForm()/setOpen(false)), ALSO clear the queue and remove the draftKey from localStorage. Be careful: the single-booking success currently routes through the ack-email/doc-assign dialogs and only fully closes in handleDocSkip/handleDocAssign/handleSaveWithoutSending/handleSendAcknowledgment terminal branches - clear the draft there (and on the batch success) so a successful save does not leave a stale draft behind. A cancelled/aborted save must NOT clear the draft.

STEP 9 - Keep the existing Booking ID provenance UI (fetching / fallback / retry) working for the CURRENT form entry. The queued entries are persisted with whatever booking_id they had, but since save-time re-resolves the id via persistBooking, that is fine. Make sure adding to the queue does not leave two entries showing the same visible id (fetch a fresh one for the new blank form as in STEP 2).
acceptance_criteria: The file compiles under `npx tsc --noEmit` (verified in CI): no type errors; BookingForm typing is consistent; no use of `any` beyond what the file already uses.
`bun run build` succeeds in CI producing dist/server/index.js and dist/server/wrangler.json.
Single-booking flow is unchanged: filling one booking and clicking Save performs the same DB insert, sheet sync, ack-email dialog, doc-assign dialog, and partial reminders as before.
Clicking 'Add another booking' with a valid form pushes it to a visible queue, clears the form for the next entry, and does not save anything yet.
Queued bookings are individually removable and editable from the dialog.

'Save all' persists every queued booking sequentially; each booking receives a DISTINCT, sequential external_booking_id from the sheet (never the same EMO id reused) because syncBookingToSheet is awaited before the next id fetch.

Partial failure during 'Save all' is surfaced (toast reports how many succeeded / failed with names), succeeded bookings are removed from the queue, failed ones remain for retry, and the draft is NOT cleared on partial failure.
Entering data (in-progress form and/or queued bookings) and refreshing the page restores both from localStorage; the draft is keyed by user id and namespaced (emo:new-booking-draft:<uid>).
JSON.parse of the stored draft is guarded; a stale/invalid/missing-field stored shape does not crash the dialog (fields fall back to defaults).
A 'Discard draft' control clears the form, the queue, and the localStorage draft; the draft otherwise persists across refreshes until the user discards it or a fully-successful save clears it.
A fully-successful save (single or batch) clears the localStorage draft; a cancelled/failed save does not.

findings: Implemented entirely in src/components/dashboard/new-booking-dialog.tsx. (1) Extracted module-level `initialForm` const + `type BookingForm = typeof initialForm`, `makeInitialForm()` (fresh EMO-BK fallback id), pure `deriveBooking(form)` (GST 18%, TDS, profit=(vo+addOn)-spPay-addOnPay, partial amounts) used by BOTH the live render (via useMemo(deriveBooking(f))), the single-save path and the batch path so math never drifts. (2) Added `persistBooking(form)` (component-scoped, uses passed form + deriveBooking, NOT outer f-bound consts): resolves id (fetches from sheet when empty or EMO-BK-*, throws on null - never writes fallback to sheet), inserts to bookings, then AWAITS syncBookingToSheet before returning. The single-save mutation is now `mutationFn: () => persistBooking(f)`; its onSuccess keeps the ack-email AlertDialog, doc-assign AlertDialog, and partial reminders exactly as before. (3) PER-BOOKING ID UNIQUENESS: `handleSaveAll` iterates with a sequential for-loop (for i=0..n, await persistBooking) - never Promise.all - so each booking's sheet row is appended (id marked used) before the next iteration calls getNextBookingIdFromSheet(), guaranteeing distinct sequential ids. IDs are NOT prefetched. (4) Queue: `const [queue,setQueue]=useState<BookingForm[]>([])`; 'Add another booking' validates via shared isFormValid(), pushes a copy, resets form + refetchNextId(); queue list renders compact rows (client, plan, city/state, total, payment type) with Edit (loads back into f, removes from queue) and Remove; only shown when queue.length>0. (5) Save button: 'Save all (N)' when queue non-empty (N counts current form only if filled+valid), else unchanged 'Save Booking'. Save-all builds [...queue, currentForm-if-filled-and-valid], accumulates succeeded/failed, does NOT abort on failure, invalidates ['bookings'] & ['booking-next-id'] once. PARTIAL FAILURE: keeps failed forms in the queue (drops succeeded), keeps the draft, toasts 'Saved X, failed Y (names)...'; only on full success clears queue+form+draft and closes. (6) BATCH POST-SAVE: one summary toast, NO N stacked ack-email/doc-assign modals (documented in code comment - those were designed for a single booking); still schedules per-booking partial-payment balance reminders via shared scheduleBalanceReminders(form,id,uuid) (silent supabase.from('reminders').insert, guarded when uuid null). (7) DRAFT: namespaced per-user key `emo:new-booking-draft:<user.id>` (anon fallback), versioned shape {v:1,form,queue}. Save effect is debounced ~400ms, writes only when queue non-empty or form filled (else removes key), wrapped in try/catch. Restore effect runs once per key, JSON.parse in try/catch, validates typeof object + v===1 + form object + Array.isArray(queue), merges each form field-by-field over initialForm defaults (mergeForm tolerates missing/extra/wrong-typed fields, coerces payment_type), re-applies current user's sales_agent identity, toasts 'Restored your saved booking draft' once. Keyed strictly by current user's key. (8) 'Discard draft' ghost/destructive button shown when queue.length>0 or form filled; window.confirm when a queue exists; clears queue+form+localStorage. (9) Draft cleared on ALL single-save terminal branches (handleDocSkip, handleDocAssign, handleSaveWithoutSending, handleSendAcknowledgment's no-uuid branch, onSuccess no-email-no-uuid branch) and on full batch success; a cancelled/failed save never clears it. VERIFICATION: could NOT run npx tsc --noEmit or bun run build in-sandbox (INTEGRATIONS_ONLY, npm 403); verified by careful code inspection - BookingForm typing consistent, no leftover outer-scope derived consts inside persistBooking, sequential for-await confirmed, localStorage guarded + shape-validated + user-keyed. Final validation delegated to CI on the PR. REVIEW-FIX PASS (2026-09-03, review 103832, all in new-booking-dialog.tsx): (#1 double-persist, FIXED) handleSaveAll's partial-failure branch now calls resetForm() whenever `includeCurrent` (not only when the current form succeeded). A failed current form is preserved because it is re-queued via `failedForms` (setQueue), so it lives in exactly one place; the live form is cleared to prevent it being saved twice on the next Save all. (#2 duplicate external_booking_id on soft sheet-sync failure, FIXED) The batch loop now treats `res.sheet.ok === false` as a HARD STOP: the booking's DB row is already inserted and is reported as saved, but since syncBookingToSheet returns {ok:false} WITHOUT throwing the id was never marked used in the sheet, so continuing would let getNextBookingIdFromSheet() hand back the same id and mint a duplicate. On stop we `break`, keep the not-yet-attempted entries (toPersist.slice(stop+1)) in the queue for retry (excluding the current form when it is among them, which stays live to avoid double-persist; plus any earlier hard-errored forms are retained), reset the current form only if it was already saved, and surface a clear toast (Saved N, sheet sync failed, remaining not saved, retry). Documented inline. Single-booking path is UNCHANGED (a soft sheet failure there remains just a warning; no next id to collide with). (#3 restore toast on page load, FIXED) The restore effect now early-returns when `!open` and depends on [draftKey, open], so restore + the 'Restored your saved booking draft' toast fire when the dialog opens, not on initial page mount (Dialog is always mounted). Still runs at most once per draftKey (restoredKeyRef guard); crash-safety preserved since the draft is restored into form/queue as soon as the dialog opens, before interaction. The debounced SAVE effect (gated on restoredKeyRef===draftKey) now only writes once the dialog has opened, which is correct for a draft. (#4 resolved id not written back to live form, DISPOSITION: left as-is) Persisted data and reminders use res.bookingId so DB/sheet are correct; the form resets on all terminal branches so the stale EMO-BK-* provenance display is not user-visible in practice. No change. (#5 batch skips per-booking ack-email/doc-assign modals, DISPOSITION: intentional, left as-is) Documented product trade-off to avoid N stacked dialogs; flagged to the orchestrator/user for product confirmation. Balance reminders are still scheduled per booking. VERIFICATION: could NOT run npx tsc --noEmit / bun run build / node (INTEGRATIONS_ONLY; npm 403 and node preload blocked in-sandbox). Verified by careful inspection: BookingForm typing consistent (notAttempted/remaining/failedForms are BookingForm[]), setQueue args typed, no leftover references to removed currentSucceeded, single-save path untouched. Final validation delegated to CI on the PR. REVIEW-FIX PASS v2 (2026-09-03, review 104653, all in new-booking-dialog.tsx): (ISSUE A, cross-save duplicate external_booking_id, FIXED) Reworked handleSaveAll's batch loop so a soft sheet-sync failure ROLLS BACK the just-inserted DB row instead of recording it as saved. The `if (!res.sheet.ok)` check now runs BEFORE scheduleBalanceReminders and before pushing to `succeeded`: when the sheet append fails we (1) delete the inserted row via `supabase.from('bookings').delete().eq('id', res.bookingUuid)` (guarded when bookingUuid is null; a delete error is captured into `rollbackNote` and surfaced in the toast but we still stop), making the sheet-derived next id genuinely unused so getNextBookingIdFromSheet() never hands it out twice; (2) do NOT count the booking as saved and do NOT schedule reminders for it (no orphan reminder rows pointing at a deleted uuid); (3) break the batch. Post-loop requeue math updated: queue is rebuilt as [...failedForms, stopForm, ...remaining] where failedForms = earlier hard-errors (indices < stop), stopForm = the rolled-back stop entry (index == stop, re-queued exactly once), remaining = not-yet-attempted entries (indices > stop) minus the current live form when it is among them. Live-form reset: `if (includeCurrent && !currentNotAttempted) resetForm()` so the current form is reset when it was the stop entry (now in queue) or an earlier failure, and left live only when it was after the stop (not attempted). Invariant holds: succeeded entries dropped; every other entry appears in exactly one place (queue OR live form), never both, never lost, never double-persisted. Fully-saved (DB+sheet) bookings before the stop remain saved. (ISSUE B, hard-stop toast messaging, FIXED) The stop-branch toast now reports the total kept-for-retry count (retryCount = failed.length + 1 stop entry + remaining.length) and, when earlier hard-failures exist, appends '(including N that failed earlier (names))', so the user understands why the queue is larger than just the not-attempted entries. Replaced the stale 'This booking's DB row IS saved' comment with the rollback rationale. Single-booking mutationFn/onSuccess/persistBooking unchanged (persistBooking still returns {bookingId, bookingUuid, sheet}); the single path still treats a soft sheet failure as a warning (no next id to collide with). Issues #1 (double-persist) and #3 (restore-on-open) preserved. VERIFICATION: could NOT run npx tsc --noEmit / bun run build / node (INTEGRATIONS_ONLY; npm 403). Verified by inspection: setQueue arg is BookingForm[] (stopForm is BookingForm), delete() returns {error} like the file's other supabase calls, res.bookingUuid is the inserted row's `id`, sheetAllOk still read in the full-success branch, both failedForms consts live in disjoint branch scopes.
